senses.definition: Finished; ended; concluded.
examples: The show isn't over until the fat lady sings.
The strawberries are over now. I picked the last few yesterday.

subsenses.definition: (botany) Of a flower: wilting or withering.

senses.definition: (informal, of an ongoing situation) Hopeless; irrecoverable.
examples: We're keeping our marriage going for the sake of the kids, but really it's over.

senses.definition: (informal) Visiting one's home or other location.
examples: My sister's over for the week.

senses.definition: Having surmounted an obstacle.
examples: The horse struggled at that fence, but it's over.

senses.definition: (informal) Having an excess in a particular respect.
examples: This steak is well over. (overcooked)
We had some complaints about short weight, so now we make sure that all our bags of potatoes are a bit over. (overweight)

senses.definition: Surplus to requirements.
examples: I made 20 cakes, but I only need 18, so there are two over.

senses.definition: (professional wrestling slang) Of a wrestler: generating a reaction from fans.
Describing a physical change of position or state.

subsenses.definition: From one position or location to another, horizontally or approximately so, or along a route visualised as "across".
examples: That vase isn't exactly central. Could you move it over a couple of inches?
I slid over to make room for him to sit down.
Please pass the chocolates over to me.
"Come over to my house and play!" — "Sure, I'll bring over a pizza."
He's driven over from Bristol.
In the future, when space travel is affordable to everyone, we'll be able to pop over to the Moon for a weekend.

subsenses.definition: Across from one side of something to the other.
examples: I need to cross the river. Can you take me over in your boat?

subsenses.definition: So as to pass above.
examples: I looked up just as a helicopter flew over.

subsenses.definition: Up one side of something, across, and then down the other side.
examples: The fence is too high. I don't think I'll be able to get over.
The boiling milk bubbled over onto the cooker top.

subsenses.definition: Across something, such as an edge, and then downwards.
examples: The car rolled to the edge of the cliff and went straight over.

subsenses.definition: From an upright position to a horizontal one.
examples: He tipped the bottle over, and the water came gushing out.
That building just fell over!

subsenses.definition: So as to fold towards or onto itself.
examples: Bend the end of that wire over to make a hook.
He bent over to touch his toes.
The leaves have curled over.

subsenses.definition: On top of something, or so as to cover something.
examples: Paint it over with a darker colour.
It's starting to cloud over.

subsenses.definition: So as to reverse up/down orientation, or otherwise change orientation by rotating.
examples: Put the card face down, and don't turn it over until I say so.
I can't sleep on my back. I have to roll over onto my side.

subsenses.definition: So as to reverse or exchange position(s).
examples: Swap those cables over. The red one should be in the left socket.

senses.definition: Expressing figurative movement from one position or state across to another.
examples: He came over to our way of thinking on the new project.
I switched over to Channel 9.
I signed the property over to him.
This advertisement doesn't clearly get the idea over.

senses.definition: Indicating a direction or location away from the speaker, usually roughly horizontally or visualised as such.
examples: I'll see you over at the club.
Look over there!

senses.definition: Thoroughly; completely; from beginning to end.
examples: Let's talk over the project at tomorrow's meeting.
Let me think that over.
I'm going to look over our department's expenses.

senses.definition: (often in compounds) To a high or excessive degree; overly; see also over-.
examples: I'm not over bothered about going to the party.

senses.definition: Beyond or in excess of what is correct or expected.
examples: The show ran ten minutes over.
We tried to stick to budget, but in the end we went twenty dollars over.

senses.definition: To a future time.
examples: Carry the shortfall over and we'll make it up tomorrow.

senses.definition: Overnight (throughout the night).
examples: We missed the last bus home so we stayed over.
Can I sleep over?

senses.definition: Indicating repetition.

subsenses.definition: (US, usually with do) Again; another time; once more; over again.
examples: I lost my paper and I had to do the entire assignment over.

subsenses.definition: Used for rhetorical effect to reinforce that something was done the stated number of times.
examples: I said the magic word three times over, and the secret door slid open.

senses.definition: See also individual entries for phrasal verbs: go over, hand over, run over, take over, win over, etc.
(cricket) A set of six legal balls bowled.
examples: Jones hit four boundaries in the first over.

senses.definition: (informal) Something having an excess of a particular property.
examples: I went fishing but caught mostly overs.

senses.definition: (gambling) A bet that a particular sporting statistic, such a points scored in a game, will be above a certain stated value.

subsenses.definition: Above; higher than; further up than.
examples: Hold the sign up over your head.

subsenses.definition: Across, from one side to the other.
examples: The guide took us over the border.

subsenses.definition: Across, so as to pass above.
examples: The vulture flew over the desert.
I looked out over the sea.

subsenses.definition: Through or around all the parts of.
examples: The estate agent showed me over the property.
We went over the cathedral and then had lunch in the cafe.

subsenses.definition: On the other side of.
examples: He lives over the road from me.
The next town is over that hill.

subsenses.definition: (informal, for 'over at/in/on') At or near (a location seen as 'across' from the speaker's location).
examples: There was a big fire over the other side of town.

examples: The dog jumped over the fence.
Let's walk over the hill to get there.
The lava bubbled up and over the rim of the crater.

subsenses.definition: Across (something) and then downwards.
examples: The car drove straight over the edge of the cliff.
I tripped over a tree root.

subsenses.definition: On top of; in such a way as to cover.
examples: Drape the fabric over the table.
There is a roof over the house.
(figuratively) A strange feeling came over me.

senses.definition: Expressing comparison.

subsenses.definition: More than (a given value, amount, limit etc.); beyond; past; exceeding.
examples: He is over a hundred years old.
It's over a hundred degrees outside.
I think I’m over my limit for calories for today.

subsenses.definition: To a greater degree than.
examples: I prefer the purple over the pink.

subsenses.definition: (in certain collocations) As compared to.
examples: Sales are down this quarter over last.

senses.definition: During or throughout (a time period).
examples: He's got grumpier over the years.
I'll have to work over the weekend.

senses.definition: Through or via (a particular transmission medium).
examples: A stern voice boomed over the loudspeaker.
The message came over FM radio.

senses.definition: Indicating relative status, authority, or power
examples: The owner's son lorded it over the experienced managers.
The prince ruled over a portion of the kingdom.

senses.definition: In a position of having overcome (a problem or issue); past; finished with; from one state to another via a hindrance that must be solved or defeated; or via a third state that represents a significant difference from the first two.
examples: We got over the engineering problems and the prototype works great.
I am over my cold and feel great again.
I know the referee made a bad call, but you have to get over it [your annoyance with the referee's decision].
She is finally over [the distress of] losing her job.
He is finally over his [distress over the loss of the relationship with his] ex-girlfriend.

senses.definition: While doing an activity involving (something), especially while consuming.
examples: We had a chat over dinner.
He fell asleep over the crossword puzle.
